notes: N = cell slots; F = (nx+1)(ny+1)(nz+1). All dense arrays include masked slots. Precision: f32 fields, u32 masks/IDs; CPU clocks/ledgers f64.
Magnet B₀ is computed once at startup. No per-step induction/self-field or thermal solve in this client. CPU/GPU control waits are not full-field transfers.
Solid arrows: explicit transfers. Green link: GPU-resident reads/writes. Chronological row order includes conditional branches detailed on sheets 2–4.

title: 2  Electrical solve — expanded PCG and data transfers
subtitle: This subactivity executes TWICE per timestep: unit-voltage basis, then motional basis; same matrix, different RHS

Set mode / voltage / target
write_params()
rows.data:
R: fluid α (from 64N fluid packet)
W: σ in DC properties (8N bytes total)

rows.cpu: Submit initial solve stages
rows.data:
R: prior high/low predictors, σ/flags, B₀/u as needed
W: work[φ,r,p,Ap], partials → scalars

rows.gpu: GPU scalar packet copied to MAP_READ staging
rows.data:
R: 64 B DC scalar buffer
CPU gets a 64 B host vector, NOT the potential field.

rows.cpu:
Enqueue 32 CG iterations
Keep accepted-field data on GPU.
rows.gpu:
apply_operator: Ap = A p
workgroup dot products
rows.data:
R: σ, flags, neighboring p
W: work.Ap, partial p·Ap

rows.cpu:
No host scalar transfer
inside these 5 kernels
rows.data:
GPU reductions set CG coefficients.
R/W: φ high/low, r, p, Ap; scratch / scalars

rows.cpu:

No → row 04; yes → row 07
rows.data:

No full potential/field download.

rows.cpu:
If candidate-converged:
request independent residual
rows.data:
R: σ, neighbor potential high/low, motional RHS
W: true-residual dot products → scalar buffer

rows.cpu:
True residual passes?
Else tighten target and continue.
rows.data: R: true-residual scalars only

rows.cpu:
Current-conservation test
Unit relative gate; motion mixed gate
rows.data:
R: terminal faces / neighbors, σ, φ high/low, u×B₀
W: net and absolute terminal-flux sums

rows.cpu:
Accept basis? Else tighten → row 04.
Cap / nonfinite → error.
rows.data:
R: flux scalars only. Residual and current gates
are both required; changing precision is not free.

rows.cpu: Read physical basis port current
rows.data:
R: σ, potential, B₀, u
W: full 64N DC output packet + power/port sums

rows.cpu: Return basis scalar results
rows.data:
R: current potential high / correction low
W: predictor vec4<f32> (16N bytes)

rows.cpu:
After BOTH bases: compute V
Then collect_fields(V) once more.
rows.data:
Final 64N packet overwrites unit/motion packets.
No new third PCG solve; only field reconstruction.

notes: Core work = vec4<f32> × N; predictors = vec4<f32> × N with separate unit/motion low words. σ + packed flags = vec2<f32> × N.
Current V5 large-grid path: each ≤5-command chunk is submitted and fenced. Fence waits have NO payload; scalar readbacks happen only at explicit checks.
Smaller-grid path batches commands without those per-chunk fences. Residual polling still occurs after 32 CG iterations. Cap/failure exits the research run.

notes: MG V-cycle = diagonal-start + restriction down levels; 8 coarse relaxation sweeps; prolongation and smoothing back up. Matrix/physics remain on the uniform fine grid.
V5 large-grid workaround fences EACH fluid/MG stage; waits transfer no fields. Normal smaller-grid MG encodes 8 CG iterations in a batch.
A phase-topology change can trigger CPU anchor rebuilding (sheet 4). In the present fixed-solid air+liquid case, moving α normally leaves the active fluid mask unchanged.

notes: Checkpoints preserve accepted solver state for error handling; disk files are separate saved observations. No disk read/write is required inside CG iterations.
Data precision: GPU packets f32; masks/flags u32; CPU ledgers f64. Every GPU→CPU readback uses a GPU staging copy + map/wait + host vector.
Both the force refresh and the two fluid projection completions materialise fluid packets/diagnostics. None of those resident packets move to CPU merely because they are called “display fields”.
